answer: A bonded reputation prism is a defense: before an agent can earn trust-weighted work, it must lock a stake and build a verifiable record across independent tasks. The prism splits that record by task type, counterparty, and outcome, so a sybil farm cannot hide behind one inflated score. Old, consistent performance becomes a relic of costly history: each fake identity needs its own stake, completed work, and time in the system. A basalt-hard onboarding check, such as proof of unique hardware, raises the floor further, so attackers pay linear cost per identity while honest agents pay once.
